title: Primary prevention that lowers incidence of a major disorder

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a safe intervention that substantially and durably reduces the first onset of a specified major psychiatric disorder. Its defining outcome is fewer new cases in an identified population over a meaningful period. Schizophrenia, bipolar disorder and severe depression are possible targets within the concept's scope, but the supplied evidence concerns prevention of first-episode psychosis among people at clinical high risk; it does not demonstrate prevention across those disorders.

People at clinical high risk for psychosis can be identified through specific psychometric interviews as a group with elevated subsequent risk. Intervention in this group is described technically as indicated prevention: participants may already experience symptoms, even though they have not developed first-episode psychosis. Thus, the retained title's use of primary prevention refers to preventing first onset and should not imply that every recipient is symptom-free or that the intervention must be delivered to the general population.

Conceptual synthesis: an early, detectable and interruptible causal antecedent would offer one route to this capability. Discovering a necessary causal step is not an established prerequisite. The concept is defined by a convincing preventive outcome, whether achieved through a specific biological mechanism, several modifiable risk pathways or another effective intervention.

significance.text: Psychotic disorders impose substantial disability, making prevention of first onset a major clinical goal. Treating an established disorder cannot prevent that person's first onset, although treatment may have other preventive consequences. An effective intervention before onset would add a capability that treatment after onset cannot provide: fewer people developing the disorder during the period observed.

Impact synthesis: a safe intervention that substantially and durably prevented schizophrenia, bipolar disorder or severe depression could reasonably be compared in significance to a vaccine achievement. This is an analogy about the value of preventing disease, not a claim of shared biology, an assertion that such an intervention exists or a prediction of its eventual effectiveness. Success against one specified disorder or in one high-risk population would not establish prevention of other psychiatric disorders.

Conditional downstream possibilities include lower demand for acute care, fewer disruptions to education and employment, and reduced disability burden. Their magnitude would depend on absolute benefit, population coverage, safety, accessibility and persistence of protection. Fewer onsets over three years would not establish lifelong avoidance of illness or quantify lifetime disability savings. Nor would prevention itself repair disability in people with established illness; those outcomes require separate evidence.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is a safe intervention that produces a clinically substantial, sustained reduction in first onset compared with credible alternative care or an appropriate population control. The supplied psychosis review documents an unmet intervention goal: the tested active interventions did not show a sustained, robust advantage over their respective controls. This finding does not establish that prevention is impossible or that existing care has no preventive effect.

A central challenge is identifying whom to treat and when. The review reports approximately 20 percent transition to psychosis within two years among clinical-high-risk populations, so many people receiving a preventive intervention would not develop psychosis within that interval. Safety and treatment burden therefore matter alongside efficacy. This group-level transition rate does not, by itself, measure the accuracy of individual prognoses or show that people who do not transition have no clinical needs.

The scientific and trial-design barriers include heterogeneous high-risk populations, potentially different causal pathways, active control conditions that may themselves help, and limited long-term outcome data. A useful intervention must reach a modifiable process early enough to change onset risk, while a convincing evaluation must distinguish its added benefit from the effects of background care. The review allows that heterogeneity and effective control care could obscure preventive effects; lack of demonstrated superiority is therefore narrower than evidence that all approaches are ineffective.

Engineering synthesis: practical deployment would also require a feasible identification pathway, reliable delivery and adherence, and consistent detection of new cases across treated and comparison populations. Follow-up must be long enough to distinguish sustained incidence reduction from temporary postponement, while adverse effects must be assessed in everyone exposed, including those who would not otherwise develop the disorder.

current_state.text: The World Psychiatric Association Preventive Psychiatry section's review by Minichino and colleagues, published on February 14, 2025, included 24 randomized trials involving 3,236 participants at clinical high risk for psychosis. Its literature search extended through November 28, 2023. Across the investigated interventions, including psychological approaches, antipsychotics and omega-3 fatty acids, it found no evidence of a sustained, robust advantage over their respective controls on transition to psychosis, symptoms or functioning. This is a dated comparative synthesis, not a demonstration that every intervention or every form of care has no preventive effect.

For cognitive behavioral therapy at 12 months, the pooled odds ratio for transition was 0.64, with a 95 percent confidence interval of 0.39–1.06. The interval includes no difference, leaving uncertainty about benefit. A pooled 18-month estimate based on three trials favored therapy, but the newest large trials did not contribute data at that time point, and later estimates did not show superiority. The 18-month finding therefore does not establish sustained preventive efficacy.

Individual trials of integrated psychotherapy and transcranial magnetic stimulation reported positive transition findings that require further confirmation. These findings preserve possible avenues for progress without establishing a broadly reproducible preventive capability. The review's omega-3 analyses did not establish a durable preventive advantage; estimates at 6 months, 12 months and beyond 36 months were nonsignificant. Sparse long-term data and wide confidence intervals limit how strongly absence of benefit can be inferred.

The research notes describe a February 26, 2024 network meta-analysis as reporting a protective omega-3 signal. That assertion remains unverified in the supplied materials: the source index contains a URL but no captured text or artifact, and the notes state that its full text was not opened and its author list was not confirmed. Its content, methods and relationship to the later pairwise synthesis cannot be assessed here. This access limitation is not evidence that the reported signal is false, but it prevents treating the alleged disagreement as resolved.

The 2025 review summarized two-year transition risk as 0.20, with a 95 percent confidence interval of 0.19–0.21. This supports elevated group-level risk; it does not independently establish weak individual prognostic performance. Longer-term intervention effectiveness remained incompletely assessed because most trials did not report outcomes beyond 12 months. The supplied review assessed the full main article, but not linked supplements or figure images. No freshness search was supplied to establish developments through November 1, 2026, so these results should not be read as an exhaustive account of evidence available on that date.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: a preregistered randomized trial, or a population intervention with a preregistered control and a credible design for causal inference, showing a sustained reduction in incidence of a specified major disorder over at least three years. The disorder, target population, intervention, comparator, onset definition and follow-up plan should be specified prospectively. Comparable case ascertainment across groups is essential; preregistration alone does not make an observational comparison causal.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed clinical-importance criterion: report absolute incidence, absolute risk reduction, uncertainty, adverse effects and the population reached. The number of cases prevented should matter clinically, rather than merely yield a statistically significant relative effect. A reduction large enough to plausibly change service demand and disability burden is a useful ambition, but those consequences require direct measurement or justified estimation. Neither an 80 percent success rate nor any other fixed percentage is adopted as an authoritative threshold.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed clinical-importance criterion

completion_criteria.text: Proposed durability criterion: a short delay in transition that disappears by two years would not satisfy this record's goal. At least three years of follow-up is a proposed minimum, not an established professional standard. Longer observation should test whether incidence remains lower or converges later. Even a successful three-year study establishes fewer onsets during that interval, not lifelong prevention.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed durability criterion

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical-boundary criteria: independent replication should establish benefit under clearly described clinical or population conditions, with acceptable harms and feasible delivery. Studies should report adherence, loss to follow-up, background care and relevant variation in benefit. Claims should remain bounded by the tested disorders, populations, settings and observation periods. Multiple successful finite studies demonstrate breadth of prevention; they cannot establish literal universality.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed reproducibility and practical-boundary criteria

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: PSY-01, Mechanism-defined diseases in place of the major syndromes, and PSY-05, Medicines designed from a confirmed human disease mechanism, could enable prevention by identifying causal subgroups or intervention targets. PSY-04 nevertheless concerns the outcome of fewer first onsets; neither a new disease classification nor a mechanism-based medicine alone demonstrates that outcome. Prevention might also succeed before a necessary causal mechanism is fully established.

Roster-based synthesis: PSY-02, A treatment that changes the course of schizophrenia, and PSY-03, Ending the relapsing course of severe mood disorders, concern changing illness after onset, whereas PSY-04 concerns reducing first onset. One intervention might meet both goals, but prevention, course modification and restoration of function require separate demonstrations. PSY-10, Reopening plasticity that can repair an established psychiatric deficit, similarly concerns repair that cannot be inferred from successful prevention. These distinctions follow the supplied titles; detailed definitions of the related entries were not provided.

Roster-based synthesis: PSY-06, A clinical instrument that reads an individual’s psychiatric state, could support identification, monitoring or outcome measurement, but a state-reading capability would need separate validation for predicting future onset. PSY-07, Reliable causal control of a core symptom by a defined circuit, might supply an intervention route; symptom control alone would not demonstrate reduced incidence of a major disorder.

Roster-based synthesis: PSY-11, Prevention of post-traumatic stress disorder by blocking consolidation, addresses a specific prevention window following trauma, distinct from the broader first-onset goal here. PSY-08, Selective and durable modification of a pathological memory, concerns a memory-level capability that might overlap with some trauma interventions without itself establishing disorder prevention. The exact boundaries remain provisional because only the roster titles and the research's description of the post-trauma window were supplied.

Roster-based synthesis: PSY-09, A time-limited reset of severe addiction, targets an established disorder rather than first onset. PSY-12, A session-level amplifier that lets brief psychotherapy match a full course, concerns treatment efficiency. Either could share methods with a preventive intervention, but resetting addiction or shortening psychotherapy would not by itself meet PSY-04's incidence-reduction criterion.

change_log.change: Preserved PSY-04 and its title while defining the capability as a substantial, durable reduction in first onset.
change_log.reason: The identity remains coherent despite corrections to supporting assertions; the innovation has not been demonstrated by the supplied evidence.

change_log.change: Reframed discovery of a necessary causal antecedent as one possible route to prevention.
change_log.reason: The supplied review establishes an unmet preventive goal but does not establish that identifying a necessary causal step is required.

change_log.change: Explained that clinical-high-risk intervention is indicated prevention and can involve already symptomatic participants.
change_log.reason: This preserves the scientific distinction between prevention of first-episode psychosis and intervention in a wholly symptom-free population.

change_log.change: Restricted the evidence claims to clinical-high-risk psychosis populations and comparative intervention effects.
change_log.reason: The supplied synthesis does not demonstrate prevention across schizophrenia, bipolar disorder and severe depression, and active controls may themselves provide benefit.

change_log.change: Retained trial counts, participant counts and the CBT estimate; specified the search cutoff and corrected the interpretation of the 18-month result.
change_log.reason: The favorable 18-month estimate pooled three trials, omitted the newest large trials at that time point and did not establish durable efficacy.

change_log.change: Included positive individual integrated-psychotherapy and transcranial magnetic stimulation findings alongside their need for confirmation.
change_log.reason: The overall synthesis should not erase potentially useful signals from individual trials.

change_log.change: Preserved the reported 2024 omega-3 signal as an unverified assertion and separated it from the supported findings of the 2025 synthesis.
change_log.reason: The network-analysis source has no supplied text or captured artifact; missing access neither confirms nor disproves the assertion.

change_log.change: Removed the inference that a roughly 20 percent transition rate proves weak individual prognosis.
change_log.reason: A group-level incidence estimate is not itself a measure of individual predictive performance.

change_log.change: Qualified the vaccine analogy, treatment comparison and claims about lifetime prevention and disability.
change_log.reason: The analogy is an impact judgment; finite follow-up establishes observed incidence reduction, and prevention does not establish repair of existing disability.

change_log.change: Expanded the proposed completion criteria to cover causal inference, absolute benefit, harms, comparable ascertainment, replication and deployment boundaries.
change_log.reason: These make success assessable while keeping the three-year duration and clinical-importance threshold explicitly proposed.

change_log.change: Integrated roster relationships without merging entries and retained source-access and freshness limitations.
change_log.reason: Only related-concept titles were supplied, and neither the uninspected materials nor developments after the dated search can be inferred.

unresolved_issues: The 2024 network meta-analysis's identity, methods, omega-3 findings and relationship to the 2025 pairwise synthesis remain unassessed because no source text or artifact was supplied.
Evidence developments after the November 28, 2023 search cutoff have not been comprehensively assessed; the supplied materials do not establish the state of the field as of November 1, 2026.
The durability of intervention effects remains uncertain because long-term follow-up was sparse; nonsignificant estimates do not establish absence of clinically meaningful benefit.
The positive individual integrated-psychotherapy and transcranial magnetic stimulation findings require confirmation before supporting a reproducible preventive capability.

The supplied evidence does not establish preventive effectiveness for bipolar disorder or severe depression, or equate prevention of first-episode psychosis with prevention of a specific eventual diagnosis such as schizophrenia.
The main article's linked supplements and figure images were not inspected in the supplied review.
A clinically meaningful absolute-benefit threshold and the appropriate follow-up duration require justification for the chosen disorder, population and intervention; three years remains a proposal.
Detailed definitions of the related roster entries were not supplied, so their exact scope and overlaps remain provisional.
